name: Burpee
pattern: Squat down, jump the feet back to a plank, jump them back in, then jump up: a full-body conditioning loop.
setup: Stand with feet hip width, arms by your sides.
Clear space of your body length in front of you.

steps.text: Squat and place your hands flat on the floor just in front of your feet.
Jump your feet back into a straight plank, body in one line.
Jump your feet back in under your hips.
Stand and jump up, arms reaching overhead; land softly into the next rep.

cues.cue: Straight plank: hips not sagging or piked.
cues.why: The trunk muscles hold the spine straight in the plank; a sag loads the lower back.

cues.cue: Land the jump softly, knees bent.
cues.why: Soft, bent-knee landings lower impact force.

cues.cue: Hands flat, shoulder width, under your shoulders in the plank.
cues.why: Keeps the push-up and plank stable and the wrists loaded evenly.

cues.cue: Keep a steady pace you can hold.
cues.why: Burpee intervals drive oxygen uptake and heart rate to vigorous levels; form fails before fitness does.

breathing: Breathe out as you jump back and as you jump up; keep a steady rhythm.

tempo.note: About 2-4 s per rep; in intervals, as many good reps as you can.

mistakes.name: Hips sag in the plank
mistakes.looks: The lower back dips when the feet land behind you.
mistakes.fix: Brace before the feet land; step back instead of jumping if needed.

mistakes.name: Stiff jump landing
mistakes.looks: Straight legs and a loud landing after the jump.
mistakes.fix: Land on the balls of your feet and sink into the next squat.

mistakes.name: Rounded back squat
mistakes.looks: Legs stay straight and the back curls to reach the floor.
mistakes.fix: Bend the knees and sit down to the floor.
mistakes.why: Many rounded reps add up on the lower back.

safety: Low impact: step the feet back and in, skip the jump.
Wrist pain: hands on a bench or fists.
Stop and walk if you feel dizzy; burpee sets push heart rate very high.

variants.change: Add a push-up in the plank.
Jump the feet wide and back in (a jumping jack) in the plank or at the top.
No jump, step back and in: about 3.8 MET (moderate calisthenics, 02022).
Hands on the weights; often finished with a clean or press.
Finish with a jump over an object, onto a box or forward.
Turn in the air on the jump.

subtypes.name: Burpee with push-up
subtypes.change: Chest to the floor in a push-up at the plank, then press up.

subtypes.name: Squat thrust or silent burpee
subtypes.change: Step or jump the feet back and in, then just stand up (no jump).

motion.basis: Plank stiffness from howarth2008; landing from padua2009; intensity from gist2014 and ratamess2015 (burpee VO2 about 23 ml/kg/min in sets of 10). Keyframe angles are estimates. MET 7.5 is Compendium 02020, which names burpees; HIIT 11.0 (02214).

sources.cite: Gist NH et al. Comparison of responses to two high-intensity intermittent exercise protocols. J Strength Cond Res. 2014.
Ratamess NA et al. Comparison of the acute metabolic responses to traditional resistance, body-weight, and battling rope exercises. J Strength Cond Res. 2015.

Padua DA et al. The Landing Error Scoring System (LESS) is a valid and reliable clinical assessment tool of jump-landing biomechanics: the JUMP-ACL study. Am J Sports Med. 2009;37(10):1996-2002.
